title: Everton boss David Moyes hopeful of having Jarrad Branthwaite fit for Arsenal
content:
Everton manager David Moyes is hopeful of having key defender Jarrad Branthwaite fit for Saturday’s trip to title-chasing Arsenal.

The 23-year-old was substituted 83 minutes into the recent home victory over Burnley, something Moyes put down to “fatigue” in his post-match conference.

Branthwaite also missed last week’s warm weather training camp in Portugal as a precaution, with Everton looking to manage him carefully after his injury troubles over the past 12 months.

The central defender spent the first half of the season on the sidelines with a hamstring injury and underwent surgery in October on the issue following what Everton described as a “complication” in his rehabilitation.

But Moyes is optimistic that Branthwaite will be available for the visit to the Emirates Stadium.

“I’m hoping everyone is fine. Jarrad we think will be ok,” the Scot said in his pre-match press conference on Friday.

“We had to leave him out for one of the games (Fulham) and there was a bit of criticism because we changed the team around for different reasons. But it was mainly because we couldn’t play him at the time.

“But he’s now (been) back long enough. We played him Saturday-Tuesday, also partly because we had the best part of a 10-day rest and recovery period.

“I think there are times when you have to look after the players. The length of Jarrad’s injury meant we were always going to have to be mindful of it.

“He plays a big part, is a really good player and we want him fit for every game. But we also have to take (medical) advice at different times.”

Everton are in eighth place ahead of Saturday’s game, five points off Chelsea in fifth.
